nodes.label: Outbound Invoicing and the Connector Seam
ADR-0151
nodes.rationale: A connector call differs from every prior governed act: its answer comes from a third party over a network and fails in ways a rate-card lookup never does, so failure handling lives in exactly one place.

nodes.label: Connector
nodes.rationale: The one piece of code that speaks to a given outside service, so that service failure modes are handled in exactly one place rather than wherever a button raises an invoice.

nodes.label: ConnectorResult<T>
nodes.rationale: Five outcomes (Ok, Rejected, Reauthorise, Unavailable, Unknown), never a thrown exception; an exception out of an implementation is a defect in it. One honest word, never a spinner hiding refused from unreachable.

nodes.label: FakeInvoicingConnector
nodes.rationale: Scriptable per call or pinned to one idempotency key; parts 2 and 3 added real connectors without changing one line of the part-1 suite.

nodes.label: Request Id as Idempotency Key
nodes.rationale: InvoiceRequest.Id itself is the idempotency key and is written into the created invoice reference field; nothing is minted, stored or lost.

nodes.label: FindByReferenceAsync
nodes.rationale: Reconciliation looks the invoice up by reference before any retry, so a timeout after Xero committed can never produce a second invoice.

nodes.label: InvoiceRequestStatus
nodes.rationale: Nine states; Unavailable is declared but never written: a failed send reverts to Draft and is not retried automatically because a request nobody can see needs a human to notice it.

nodes.label: Paid Is Read Never Set
nodes.rationale: Paid is a fact this platform reads, never computes: only RecordStatusReadingAsync writes PaidDate, called only from ReconcileAsync; asserting it here would let TempestOS disagree with the ledger that governs the money.

nodes.label: ISecretStore
nodes.rationale: Tokens live under persistence root secrets, never inside tempest.db, because tempest.db is precisely the file backed up, exported and handed to support.

nodes.label: FileSecretStore
nodes.rationale: Disclosed unencrypted fallback on non-Windows, logging a Warning naming exactly what it is.

nodes.label: Loopback Redirect Port 48131
nodes.rationale: Xero and Intuit consoles require one exact redirect URI registered ahead of time; moved from 49301 (Windows dynamic range) to 48131.

nodes.label: InvoiceReconciliationService
nodes.rationale: First real consumer of the platform IHostedService; polls every Invoicing:PollMinutes (15) via an injected TimeProvider so tests advance a fake clock; failures logged and skipped since it affects only how quickly a person finds out.

nodes.label: HTTP Outcome Mapping Table
nodes.rationale: 2xx Ok, 400/422 Rejected, 401/403 Reauthorise, 429/5xx or transport failure Unavailable.

nodes.label: DeriveExternalStatus
nodes.rationale: QuickBooks carries no single status word, so one is synthesised from Balance, TotalAmt and EmailStatus into the vocabulary InterpretStatus already matches.

nodes.label: DeriveDocNumber
nodes.rationale: QuickBooks DocNumber allows 21 characters against a 36-character id; TOS- plus seventeen hex digits, deterministic but disclosed as not a uniqueness claim.

nodes.label: StubHttpMessageHandler
nodes.rationale: Recorded responses, not a live sandbox: deterministic, fast, refusing any unscripted request, which is what lets the suite run in CI; cannot prove the real API still behaves as documented.

nodes.label: InvoicingService.ToSnapshotAsync
nodes.rationale: Resolves the client display name once, the only place in the seam that reads the organisation catalogue; connectors had matched on a catalogue id no contact list could hold.

nodes.label: One Live Request per Source
nodes.rationale: InvoicedBy is written only at Sent, so a completion hook and Raise invoice could both raise Drafts; the fix reads every live request first and refuses a second for the same source. Caught one run in two because the defect itself only sometimes had a window.

nodes.label: Five Invoice Groups
nodes.rationale: New, Available to invoice, Sent, Outstanding/Overdue, Closed replaced nine engineer-only statuses; InvoicesGroupingTests proves every status lands in exactly one.

nodes.label: PaymentTerms and DueOn
nodes.rationale: A client PaymentTerms value is frozen onto the request at Send and DueOn computed once, replacing a thirty-day guess.

nodes.label: Xero Only for This Release
nodes.rationale: PO decision 2026-09-15; QuickBooks item-reference gap deferred as P4, connector stays selectable but no v1.0.0 Work Package carries it.

nodes.label: Sending Is Sequential Not One Transaction
nodes.rationale: ExecuteWriteAsync commits one object state per call; spanning request status and line InvoicedBy links was a substrate change outside this Work Package, a disclosed cost.
